# Upstream triage + review scripts

Tooling for managing the firehose of issues + PRs on `gastownhall/beads`. Two
loops: **triage** (decide what to do) and **review** (do the PR work, resumable
across machines).

The workflow is split into three layers by **output audience** (v2 redesign,
2026-07-07, after the v1 experiment drowned readers in agent-written text):

1. **Mechanical sync** (`tri-pull`, `tri-sync`, `tri-daily`, labels) - posts
   no text anywhere; runs freely, cron-safe.
2. **Classification** (`/triage` command in Claude Code) - dispositions and
   one-line reasons into bd labels/notes, plus one short digest per run under
   `reports/triage/`. Never posts text upstream.
3. **Publication** (`tri-submit`) - the only path that posts agent-drafted
   text to upstream GitHub. Word-budgeted, distilled into a separate
   `NNNN.post.md`, and gated behind interactive terminal confirmation so
   unattended agents cannot post.

The old blanket `MYBD_ENABLE_TRIAGE=1` gate is gone; the gate now sits
exactly where the risk is (text publication), not on the whole toolkit.

On Windows, do not invoke extensionless scripts directly from PowerShell. Use
the matching `.ps1` wrapper, for example `scripts/tri-daily.ps1`, or run the
extensionless script through Git Bash.

## Daily workflow

```
1. tri-pull + tri-sync          # or /triage in Claude Code, which wraps both,
     classifies each stub (tri:* label + one-line reason), and writes a short
     digest to reports/triage/YYYY-MM-DD.md
2. review the digest / bd ready # confirm or flip dispositions:
     close / defer / claim / human / needs-info
3. tri-review <id>              # for claimed PRs: worktree + scaffolds + checks
4. edit pr-reviews/NNNN.md      # full analysis, stays local
5. distill pr-reviews/NNNN.post.md   # <=150 words, the only text posted
6. tri-submit <id> --approve    # budget-lint + confirm at terminal + post
                                #   + close bd + label upstream

For non-PR triage stubs: tri-close <id> [--reason=...]
```

Re-running `tri-pull` daily is idempotent. It only mirrors items lacking the
`triaged` label upstream and skips any already in bd (matched by `external_ref`).

Pair with `tri-sync` (below) to also auto-close bd stubs whose upstream item
has since been merged or closed.

## tri-daily (unattended Layer 2 wrapper)

1	---
2	description: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
3	allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read(*), Grep(*), Glob(*), Agent(*)
4	---
5	
6	Run the pinned triage procedure. The deliverable of triage is a DISPOSITION
7	per item plus one sentence of why - not an essay. This command exists because
8	free-form triage drowned readers in text (owner feedback, 2026-07-07). Follow
9	the procedure and the caps exactly; do not improvise extra output.
10	
11	Hard rules, non-negotiable:
12	
13	- **Never post text to upstream GitHub.** No `gh pr review`, `gh pr comment`,
14	  `gh issue comment`. Do not run `tri-submit`. The only upstream writes allowed
15	  are text-free `triaged` labels via `scripts/tri-close`.
16	- Run all bd/gh-writing steps **serially** (embedded-Dolt locking).
17	- Classification subagents are **read-only** and cheap (scout tier).
18	
19	## 1. Mechanical sync (Layer 1)
20	
21	```bash
22	scripts/tri-pull          # mirror new untriaged upstream items into bd
23	scripts/tri-sync          # close stubs whose upstream item is terminal
24	```
25	
26	Record the counts they report for the digest header. If either fails on gh
27	auth or rate limits, report and stop.
28	
29	## 2. Classify (Layer 2)
30	
31	Build the worklist: open bd stubs with a `gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN` external_ref and
32	no existing `tri:*` label:
33	
34	```bash
35	bd list --status=open --limit 0 --json \
36	  | jq -r '.[] | select(.external_ref != null and (.external_ref | test("^gh-(pr|iss)-[0-9]+$")))
37	           | select(((.labels // []) | map(startswith("tri:")) | any) | not)
38	           | "\(.id) \(.external_ref) \(.title)"'
39	```
40	
41	For each item, produce a classification with EXACTLY this shape (read-only
42	scout subagents may fetch `gh pr view` / `gh issue view` for signals; batch
43	several items per subagent):
44	
45	- `disposition`: one of `close` | `defer` | `claim` | `human` | `needs-info`
46	- `priority`: P0-P4
47	- `reason`: **max 200 characters**, one sentence
48	- `confidence`: high | medium | low
49	
50	Disposition guide: `close` = obsolete, duplicate, already-handled upstream,
51	or clearly not actionable by us; `defer` = real but not now; `claim` = we
52	should do it and the spec is clear; `human` = judgment call the owner must
53	make (contentious, social, or high-stakes); `needs-info` = cannot classify
54	from available signals.
55	
56	## 3. Record (serial)
57	
58	For each classified item, one bd update:
59	
60	```bash
61	bd update <id> --add-label "tri:<disposition>" --priority <Pn> \
62	  --append-notes "[triage $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)] <reason>"
63	```
64	
65	For `close` dispositions with **high** confidence only, also run
66	`scripts/tri-close <id> --reason="<reason>"` (closes the stub and applies the
67	text-free upstream `triaged` label). Medium/low confidence closes stay open
68	with the `tri:close` label for the owner to confirm.
69	
70	## 4. Digest (the only human-facing output)
71	
72	Write `reports/triage/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (md only, no html). Format, strictly:
73	
74	```markdown
75	# Triage digest - YYYY-MM-DD
76	
77	Pulled N new, auto-closed M terminal, classified K.
78	
79	| bd | ref | disp | P | conf | reason (<=200 chars) |
80	|----|-----|------|---|------|----------------------|
81	```
82	
83	One row per item, one line per row. After the table, at most two short
84	sections:
85	
86	- **Flagged for human** - the `human` and low-confidence items, one line each,
87	  with the single question the owner must answer.
88	- **Coverage** - anything skipped (rate limits, fetch failures, window
89	  truncation reported by tri-pull).
90	
91	The whole digest must stay under ~80 lines. If the item count would exceed
92	that, keep the flagged items as rows and collapse the rest into per-disposition
93	counts, noting the collapse in Coverage.
94	
95	## 5. Report back
96	
97	In the conversation, give ONLY: the counts line, the flagged-for-human items,
98	and the digest path. Do not restate the table. Do not close this command's
99	work with a session push unless the user asks; the digest file plus bd labels
100	are the deliverable.
101

## tri-daily (unattended Layer 2 wrapper)

```bash
scripts/tri-daily                         # run tri-pull + tri-sync once
scripts/tri-daily --pull-only             # only mirror new items in
scripts/tri-daily --sync-only             # only close upstream-terminal stubs
scripts/tri-daily --verbose               # print the same summary it logs
scripts/tri-install-cron                  # install a daily cron entry (06:17 local time)
scripts/tri-install-cron --schedule "45 5 * * *"
```

`tri-daily` is the practical machine-bound unattended path for Layer 2. It is
designed for cron:

- silent on success when nothing changed
- appends a one-line summary to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/mybd/tri-daily.log`
  when `tri-pull` creates new stubs or `tri-sync` auto-closes stale ones
- appends full diagnostics and exits non-zero on failures (`gh` auth/rate
  limit, network, command errors)

`tri-install-cron` installs or replaces a single tagged crontab entry that
`cd`s into this checkout and runs `scripts/tri-daily` once per day. This is
intentionally local-machine only; if you rotate between machines, install it on
the one that has working `gh auth`.

## tri-pull

```bash
scripts/tri-pull              # full pass: issues + PRs, limit 100 each
scripts/tri-pull --limit 30   # smaller batch
scripts/tri-pull --prs-only
scripts/tri-pull --issues-only
scripts/tri-pull --dry-run    # preview
```

Each created bd issue:
- `external_ref`: `gh-pr-NNNN` / `gh-iss-NNNN` — the structured upstream link
- `title`: the upstream title verbatim
- `description`: URL, author, created date, labels, draft flag, decision options
- `priority`: heuristic from title/body/size/age/review state
- `type`: `bug` if title starts `fix(`/`fix:`, `feature` if `feat(`/`feat:`, else `task`

Additional Layer 2 behavior now shipped in `tri-pull`:
- smarter default priority (`P0`..`P4`) for fresh bugs/perf work vs drafts, stale conflicts, and very large changes
- dependency linking for stacked PRs (`stacks on #NNNN`, `depends on #NNNN`) and PRs that close issues
- warning pass for recently closed stubs whose upstream item still lacks the `triaged` label

The classifier is still heuristic. It should get `bd ready` closer to manual
triage order, not replace human judgment.

## tri-sync

```bash
scripts/tri-sync                # close bd stubs whose upstream PR/issue is merged/closed
scripts/tri-sync --dry-run      # preview
scripts/tri-sync --prs-only
scripts/tri-sync --issues-only
scripts/tri-sync --limit 20
```

Walks open bd issues with `gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN` refs, queries `gh` for upstream
state, and closes bd stubs that are terminal upstream:

- PR `MERGED` → `bd close --reason="upstream merged: <sha7>"`
- PR `CLOSED` (not merged) → `bd close --reason="upstream closed (not merged)"`
- issue `CLOSED` → `bd close --reason="upstream closed: <stateReason>"`

Does NOT apply the `triaged` label upstream — the upstream item is already
terminal, so labeling adds noise. Each closure also gets a `tri-sync: closed
(...)` audit note on the bd issue. Idempotent; safe to run from cron alongside
`tri-pull`.

## tri-close

```bash
scripts/tri-close mybd-XXX                      # close + label upstream
scripts/tri-close mybd-XXX --reason="dupe of #1234"
scripts/tri-close mybd-XXX --skip-label         # close bd only (rare)
scripts/tri-close mybd-XXX --dry-run            # preview
```

Reads `external_ref` to know which upstream PR/issue to label. Refuses to act
on bd issues without a `gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN` ref — use `bd close` directly for
non-triage stubs.

Plain `bd close <id>` is also covered in this repo via `.beads/hooks/on_close`,
which calls `scripts/tri-label-upstream` as a best-effort async hook.

## Triage decision tree (per item in `bd ready`)

| Decision  | What to run                                              | When                                        |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tri-daily — cron-safe unattended wrapper around tri-pull + tri-sync.
#
# Intended for machine-bound daily scheduling. Behavior:
# - silent on no-op runs (no stdout/stderr on success with zero changes)
# - append a one-line summary when items are pulled or auto-closed
# - append full diagnostics on failures and exit non-zero
#
# Usage:
#   tri-daily
#   tri-daily --pull-only
#   tri-daily --sync-only
#   tri-daily --log /path/to/log
#   tri-daily --verbose

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/_tri-lib.sh"

PULL_CMD=("${TRI_PULL_CMD:-$SCRIPT_DIR/tri-pull}")
SYNC_CMD=("${TRI_SYNC_CMD:-$SCRIPT_DIR/tri-sync}")
CHECK_CMD=("${TRI_CHECK_BEADS_CONFIG_CMD:-$SCRIPT_DIR/check-beads-config}")
STATE_HOME="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
LOG_PATH="${TRI_DAILY_LOG:-$STATE_HOME/mybd/tri-daily.log}"
DO_PULL=1
DO_SYNC=1
VERBOSE=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --pull-only) DO_SYNC=0; shift;;
    --sync-only) DO_PULL=0; shift;;
    --log) LOG_PATH="$2"; shift 2;;
    --log=*) LOG_PATH="${1#--log=}"; shift;;
    --verbose) VERBOSE=1; shift;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,15p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    *) echo "tri-daily: unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_PATH")"

log_line() {
  local level="$1"
  shift
  printf '%s [%s] %s\n' "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" "$level" "$*" >>"$LOG_PATH"
}

run_step() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  local tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if "$@" >"$tmp" 2>&1; then
    cat "$tmp"
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return 0
  fi

  log_line "ERROR" "$label failed"
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    log_line "ERROR" "$label: $line"
  done <"$tmp"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  return 1
}

extract_created_count() {
  sed -n 's/^Done\. Created: \([0-9][0-9]*\), skipped.*/\1/p'
}

extract_closed_count() {
  sed -n 's/^Closed \([0-9][0-9]*\) item(s);.*/\1/p'
}

pull_created=0
sync_closed=0

run_step check-beads-config "${CHECK_CMD[@]}" --quiet >/dev/null || exit 1
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tri-install-cron — install/update a daily cron entry for tri-daily.
#
# Usage:
#   tri-install-cron
#   tri-install-cron --schedule "17 6 * * *"
#   tri-install-cron --log /tmp/tri-daily.log

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/_tri-lib.sh"

PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
SCHEDULE="${TRI_DAILY_SCHEDULE:-17 6 * * *}"
STATE_HOME="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
LOG_PATH="${TRI_DAILY_LOG:-$STATE_HOME/mybd/tri-daily.log}"
MARKER="# mybd tri-daily"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --schedule) SCHEDULE="$2"; shift 2;;
    --schedule=*) SCHEDULE="${1#--schedule=}"; shift;;
    --log) LOG_PATH="$2"; shift 2;;
    --log=*) LOG_PATH="${1#--log=}"; shift;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,9p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    *) echo "tri-install-cron: unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2;;
  esac
done

command -v crontab >/dev/null || { echo "tri-install-cron: crontab not found" >&2; exit 127; }

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_PATH")"

entry="$SCHEDULE cd '$PROJECT_ROOT' && TRI_DAILY_LOG='$LOG_PATH' '$SCRIPT_DIR/tri-daily' $MARKER"
current="$(crontab -l 2>/dev/null || true)"
filtered="$(printf '%s\n' "$current" | grep -Fv "$MARKER" || true)"

{
  printf '%s\n' "$filtered" | sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d'
---

content.text:
Short version of my opinion: **the issue analog mostly already exists but isn't turned on, and the piece that's genuinely missing is smaller than a new babysitter.** Here's what I found and what I'd do.

## What I found

**1. The mechanical layer is built but not running.** `scripts/tri-daily` (tri-pull + tri-sync, cron-safe, silent-on-noop, logs to `~/.local/state/mybd/tri-daily.log`) is exactly the issue-intake equivalent of pr-babysit's mechanical loop — but there's no crontab entry and no systemd timer for it on this machine. The pr-babysit and verify-babysit timers are live; tri-daily is only firing when someone happens to run `/triage` in a session. That log file doesn't even exist yet.

**2. Classification is actually keeping up.** All 88 open issue/PR-stub beads carry a `tri:*` label — zero untriaged. So the intake pipeline isn't the pain point right now.

**3. The real backlog is the drain, not the intake.** Of those 88: **52 are `tri:claim`** ("we should do this, spec is clear"), 28 defer, 7 human, 1 needs-info. That's the issue-side equivalent of the PR queue before you started author-clustered sweeps — triaged, sitting, nothing pulling it through.

## My opinion

**Don't build an "issue-babysit" that acts on issues autonomously.** The babysitters work because the judgment already happened and only a mechanical tail remains ("merge when green", "run the recorded verify_cmd"). Issues have no such endpoint — every next step (fix it, answer it, close it) needs judgment or posts text upstream, which your Layer 3 design deliberately human-gates. A timer can't safely own that.

What I'd do instead, in order of value:

1. **Install what exists.** Put `tri-daily` on a systemd user timer (consistent with the babysit pattern on this machine; `tri-install-cron` uses crontab, which also works but splits your scheduling story). Daily or twice-daily is plenty. Zero tokens, ~an hour of work at most, and it closes the "miss things coming in" worry for intake.

2. **Add the one genuinely missing mechanical piece: drift detection.** tri-sync only notices *terminal* upstream states (merged/closed). Nothing notices when an already-triaged issue gets new comments, a maintainer label, or an edit after we classified it — so a `tri:defer` or `tri:needs-info` stub can silently become urgent. A small `tri-drift` pass (compare upstream `updatedAt` against the triage timestamp in the bead notes, flag movers with a `tri:stale` label or by bumping them back into the untriaged worklist) fits the zero-token babysit philosophy exactly and could ride the same timer as tri-daily.

3. **Treat the 52 `tri:claim` stubs as a session pattern, not a timer.** The proven drain for PRs was author-clustered sweeps; the issue equivalent is probably *subsystem/theme-clustered* sweeps (all the sync issues in one session, all the doctor issues in another). That's a working convention plus a recurring bead, not a script.

4. **Surface the 7 `tri:human` items** — those are waiting on you specifically, and nothing currently nags about them. The drift/patrol log or the triage digest could list them until dispositioned.

If you want, I can do (1) and (2) now — install the timer and write `tri-drift` — and file a bead for the sweep pattern in (3). But I'd start with the observation that the biggest miss risk today isn't new issues arriving unseen; it's the 52 already-triaged ones nobody is draining.
yes do all 3 of those, and then help me think through how to start draining the already triaged effectively

I'll implement all three: tri-daily on a systemd timer, a new `tri-drift` detector, and the drain-pattern bead — then come back with the draining strategy. Starting by reading the existing patterns I'll mirror.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install and enable the verify-babysit systemd user timer on this machine.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
common_dir="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir)"
[[ "$common_dir" = /* ]] || common_dir="$ROOT/$common_dir"
STABLE_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$common_dir")" && pwd)"
[[ -x "$STABLE_ROOT/scripts/verify-next" ]] || { echo "stable checkout is incomplete: $STABLE_ROOT" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ ! "$STABLE_ROOT" =~ [[:space:]\"\'\\\;\|\&\$\<\>\`%] ]] || { echo "unsafe systemd path: $STABLE_ROOT" >&2; exit 1; }
UNIT_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/systemd/user"
mkdir -p "$UNIT_DIR"
root_escaped="$(printf '%s' "$STABLE_ROOT" | sed 's/[\\&|]/\\&/g')"
service_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/.verify-babysit.XXXXXX.service")"
timer_tmp="$(mktemp "$UNIT_DIR/verify-babysit.timer.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$service_tmp" "$timer_tmp"' EXIT
sed "s|@ROOT@|$root_escaped|g" "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/verify-babysit.service" >"$service_tmp"
if command -v systemd-analyze >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemd-analyze verify "$service_tmp"; fi
chmod 0644 "$service_tmp"
install -m 0644 "$ROOT/scripts/systemd/verify-babysit.timer" "$timer_tmp"
mv -f "$service_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/verify-babysit.service"
mv -f "$timer_tmp" "$UNIT_DIR/verify-babysit.timer"
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now verify-babysit.timer
systemctl --user list-timers verify-babysit.timer --no-pager
[Unit]
Description=Verify-queue consumer (zero-token babysitter for queued local verification jobs)

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=PATH=%h/.local/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
# Suite commands may carry their own long timeouts (e.g. go test -timeout 90m);
# give verify-next headroom past those instead of killing mid-suite.
Environment=VERIFY_TIMEOUT=100m
# bd resolves its database from the cwd; without this the run sees no queue.
WorkingDirectory=@ROOT@
ExecStart="@ROOT@/scripts/verify-next"
TimeoutStartSec=110min
# Full Beads/Dolt suites are process and disk heavy; stay polite on a
# workstation that may have interactive sessions running.
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle
[Unit]
Description=Run verify-next every 15 minutes

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*:07/15
RandomizedDelaySec=45
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

# shellcheck shell=bash
# _tri-lib.sh — shared helpers for tri-* scripts.
#
# Source from script: . "$(dirname "$0")/_tri-lib.sh"

TRI_UPSTREAM="${TRI_UPSTREAM:-gastownhall/beads}"
TRI_WORKTREE_BASE="${TRI_WORKTREE_BASE:-$HOME/dev/mybd-tri}"
TRI_PROJECT_ROOT="${TRI_PROJECT_ROOT:-$(git -C "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
TRI_BD_MAIN="${TRI_BD_MAIN:-$TRI_PROJECT_ROOT/bd-main}"
TRI_REVIEWS_DIR="${TRI_REVIEWS_DIR:-$TRI_PROJECT_ROOT/_working_on/pr-reviews}"

TRI_POST_MAX_WORDS="${TRI_POST_MAX_WORDS:-150}"

tri_die() { echo "${0##*/}: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# Confirmation gate for posting agent-authored TEXT to upstream GitHub.
# Mirroring, labels, and local reports run freely; text posts require a human
# at a terminal. Confirmation is read from /dev/tty specifically so that
# unattended agents (no controlling terminal) cannot pass the gate.
# TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST=1 is the deliberate, owner-only escape hatch.
tri_confirm_post() {
  local body_file="$1" target="$2"
  if [[ "${TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST=1 — skipping interactive confirmation" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  # -r/-w /dev/tty pass even with no controlling terminal; actually open it.
  if ! { : </dev/tty; } 2>/dev/null; then
    tri_die "posting text to $target requires an interactive terminal.
Agents: leave the distilled post file in place and hand off to a human.
Humans automating deliberately: TRI_ALLOW_UNATTENDED_POST=1"
  fi
  {
    echo
    echo "── Exact body that will be posted to $target ──"
    cat "$body_file"
    echo "── end body ──"
    printf 'Post this? Type "post" to confirm, anything else aborts: '
  } >/dev/tty
  local answer=""
  IFS= read -r answer </dev/tty || true
  [[ "$answer" == "post" ]] || tri_die "not confirmed — nothing posted"
}

# True (exit 0) iff the body has non-whitespace content OUTSIDE HTML comment
# blocks. Line-prefix checks are not enough: the tri-review post scaffold is a
# multi-line <!-- ... --> whose interior lines look like content.
tri_body_has_content() {
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      while (1) {
        if (!inc) {
          s = index(line, "<!--")
          if (s) {
            if (substr(line, 1, s - 1) ~ /[^ \t]/) found = 1
            line = substr(line, s + 4); inc = 1
          } else {
            if (line ~ /[^ \t]/) found = 1
            break
          }
        } else {
          e = index(line, "-->")
          if (e) { line = substr(line, e + 3); inc = 0 } else break
        }
      }
    }
    END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }
  ' "$1"
}

# Stdin filter: drop HTML comment spans, keeping text before/after them.
tri_strip_html_comments() {
  awk '
    {
      line = $0; out = ""
      while (1) {
        if (!inc) {
          s = index(line, "<!--")
          if (s) { out = out substr(line, 1, s - 1); line = substr(line, s + 4); inc = 1 }
          else { out = out line; break }
        } else {
          e = index(line, "-->")
          if (e) { line = substr(line, e + 3); inc = 0 } else break
        }
      }
      print out
    }
  '
}

# Count the words of a GitHub-facing body, excluding fenced code blocks and
# HTML comments (invisible on GitHub), and fail if over budget. Prints the
# count on success. An unterminated fence would silently exclude everything
# after it, so refuse it instead of undercounting.
tri_word_budget() {
  local body_file="$1" max_words="$2"
  local fences words
  fences="$(grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)' "$body_file" || true)"
  if (( ${fences:-0} % 2 != 0 )); then
    tri_die "unterminated code fence in $body_file - close it before posting"
  fi
  words="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/{in_code=!in_code; next} !in_code' "$body_file" \
    | tri_strip_html_comments | wc -w)"
  if (( words > max_words )); then
    tri_die "body is $words words, budget is $max_words: $body_file
Keep only what changes the maintainer's action: verdict plus top findings.
The full analysis stays in the local review note, not the upstream post."
  fi
  echo "$words"
}

tri_require() {
  for cmd in "$@"; do
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null || tri_die "$cmd not on PATH"
  done
}

# Returns the bd issue's external_ref (e.g., gh-pr-3482), or empty string.
tri_external_ref() {
  local bd_id="$1"
  bd show "$bd_id" --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[0].external_ref // empty'
}

# Parses a gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN ref into "kind num" (e.g., "pr 3482"). Returns 1 if not matched.
tri_parse_ref() {
  local ref="$1"
  if [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh-(pr|iss)-([0-9]+)$ ]]; then
    echo "${BASH_REMATCH[1]} ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Worktree path for PR number.
tri_worktree_path() { printf '%s/%s\n' "$TRI_WORKTREE_BASE" "$1"; }

# Review note path for PR number (full local analysis, never posted).
tri_review_note_path() { printf '%s/%s.md\n' "$TRI_REVIEWS_DIR" "$1"; }

# Distilled upstream post path for PR number (the ONLY file tri-submit posts).
tri_post_note_path() { printf '%s/%s.post.md\n' "$TRI_REVIEWS_DIR" "$1"; }

# Branch name convention.
tri_branch_name() { printf 'pr-%s-review\n' "$1"; }

# Append a timestamped + machine-tagged note to a bd issue.
tri_log_note() {
  local bd_id="$1" msg="$2"
  local stamp host
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  host="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
  bd update "$bd_id" --append-notes="[$stamp $host] $msg" >/dev/null
}

# Resolve a bd-id (or short pr num) to a bd-id. Accepts:
#   mybd-XXX           → as-is (validated by bd show)
#   mybd-XXX.N[.M...]  → child/grandchild ids (dotted numeric suffix)
#   #NNNN  / NNNN      → searches bd by external_ref gh-pr-NNNN
tri_resolve_bd_id() {
  local input="$1"
  if [[ "$input" =~ ^mybd-[a-z0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ ]]; then
    echo "$input"
    return 0
  fi
  local num="${input#\#}"
  if [[ "$num" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    local id
    id="$(bd list --limit 0 --json 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg ref "gh-pr-$num" '.[] | select(.external_ref == $ref) | .id' \
      | head -n1)"
    [[ -n "$id" ]] || tri_die "no bd issue with external_ref=gh-pr-$num"
    echo "$id"
    return 0
  fi
  tri_die "unrecognized id: $input (expected mybd-XXX or PR number)"
}

# Print a formatted line of "key: value" diagnostics, padded.
tri_kv() { printf '  %-22s %s\n' "$1:" "$2"; }

# Lint a Markdown body before posting it to GitHub. This catches the two
# recurring shell-handoff mistakes that GitHub will render badly.
tri_lint_gh_body() {
  local body_file="$1"
  [[ -f "$body_file" ]] || tri_die "GitHub body file not found: $body_file"

  local failed=0
  if grep -nF '\n' "$body_file" >&2; then
    echo "GitHub body contains literal \\n sequences; write real newlines and use --body-file" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if grep -nE '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])GH#[0-9]+' "$body_file" >&2; then
    echo "GitHub body contains GH# refs; use #1234 or owner/repo#1234 for GitHub autolinks" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  [[ "$failed" == 0 ]] || tri_die "GitHub body lint failed: $body_file"
}

# Normalize safe GitHub body patterns in-place. This intentionally only changes
# same-repo shorthand refs; literal \n needs a human/template fix.
tri_normalize_gh_body() {
  local body_file="$1"
  [[ -f "$body_file" ]] || tri_die "GitHub body file not found: $body_file"
  perl -0pi -e 's/(^|[^[:alnum:]_])GH#([0-9]+)/$1#$2/g' "$body_file"
}

result.output:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tri-sync — mirror terminal upstream state into bd: close stubs whose
# upstream PR/issue is merged or closed.
#
# Complement to tri-pull (which brings new items *in*). Walks all open bd
# issues with gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN external_refs, queries gh for upstream state,
# and closes the bd stub if upstream is terminal. Captures merge SHA or
# close reason in the bd close reason for traceability.
#
# Does NOT apply the upstream 'triaged' label — that's tri-close's job for
# active triage decisions. Upstream items here are already terminal.
#
# Usage:
#   tri-sync                  # full pass: PRs + issues
#   tri-sync --prs-only       # PRs only
#   tri-sync --issues-only    # issues only
#   tri-sync --dry-run        # preview, no writes
#   tri-sync --limit N        # cap items processed (default: no cap)
#
# Idempotent: re-running closes only newly-terminal items.

set -euo pipefail

. "$(dirname "$0")/_tri-lib.sh"

UPSTREAM="$TRI_UPSTREAM"
DRY_RUN=0
LIMIT=0
DO_PRS=1
DO_ISSUES=1

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift;;
    --prs-only) DO_ISSUES=0; shift;;
    --issues-only) DO_PRS=0; shift;;
    --limit) LIMIT="$2"; shift 2;;
    --limit=*) LIMIT="${1#--limit=}"; shift;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,21p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    *) tri_die "unknown arg: $1";;
  esac
done

tri_require bd gh jq

# Emit one "<bd-id> <ref>" line per open bd issue with a gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN ref.
list_open_with_refs() {
  bd list --status=open --limit 0 --json 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.[] | select(.external_ref != null and (.external_ref | test("^gh-(pr|iss)-[0-9]+$"))) | "\(.id) \(.external_ref)"'
}

closed_count=0
skipped_count=0
processed=0

while read -r bd_id ref; do
  [[ -z "$bd_id" ]] && continue
  if [[ "$LIMIT" -gt 0 && "$processed" -ge "$LIMIT" ]]; then
    break
  fi
  processed=$((processed + 1))

  parsed="$(tri_parse_ref "$ref")" || { skipped_count=$((skipped_count + 1)); continue; }
  read -r kind num <<<"$parsed"

  if [[ "$kind" == "pr" && "$DO_PRS" == 0 ]]; then continue; fi
  if [[ "$kind" == "iss" && "$DO_ISSUES" == 0 ]]; then continue; fi

  if [[ "$kind" == "pr" ]]; then
    json="$(gh pr view "$num" --repo "$UPSTREAM" --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,url 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -z "$json" ]] && { echo "  ? $bd_id ($ref): gh pr view failed, skipping" >&2; skipped_count=$((skipped_count + 1)); continue; }
    state="$(echo "$json" | jq -r '.state')"
    case "$state" in
      MERGED)
        sha="$(echo "$json" | jq -r '.mergeCommit.oid // empty' | cut -c1-7)"
        reason="upstream merged${sha:+: $sha}"
        ;;
      CLOSED)
        reason="upstream closed (not merged)"
        ;;
      *)
        continue
        ;;
    esac
  else
    json="$(gh issue view "$num" --repo "$UPSTREAM" --json state,stateReason,url 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -z "$json" ]] && { echo "  ? $bd_id ($ref): gh issue view failed, skipping" >&2; skipped_count=$((skipped_count + 1)); continue; }
    state="$(echo "$json" | jq -r '.state')"
    [[ "$state" != "CLOSED" ]] && continue
    state_reason="$(echo "$json" | jq -r '.stateReason // empty')"
    if [[ -n "$state_reason" && "$state_reason" != "null" ]]; then
      reason="upstream closed: ${state_reason,,}"
    else
      reason="upstream closed"
    fi
  fi

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == 1 ]]; then
    echo "  ✓ $bd_id ($ref): would close — $reason"
  else
    bd close "$bd_id" --reason="$reason" >/dev/null
    tri_log_note "$bd_id" "tri-sync: closed ($reason)"
    echo "  ✓ $bd_id ($ref): closed — $reason"
  fi
  closed_count=$((closed_count + 1))
done < <(list_open_with_refs)

if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == 1 ]]; then
  echo "DRY-RUN: would close $closed_count item(s); skipped $skipped_count; checked $processed"
else
  echo "Closed $closed_count item(s); skipped $skipped_count; checked $processed"
fi
